2027-07-01.title: Thursday of the Thirteenth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son
Not to us, O Lord, but to your name give glory
Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven
2027-07-01.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 13 (Year I). The first reading continues the story of Abraham with its greatest test, the binding of Isaac. The Gospel of the weekdays of Weeks 13 and 14 follows the mighty works of Matthew 8–9. In popular devotion July is the month of the Most Precious Blood. In Kerala the first monsoon rains of the month of Mithunam are still falling. Liturgical colour: green.
2027-07-01.verse: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
theo: Today's first reading is one of the most demanding chapters of the Bible. “After these things God tested Abraham.” The old man has waited twenty-five years for Isaac, has sent Ishmael away at God's command, and now hears the voice again: “Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering.” Notice how slowly the command tightens: your son, your only son, Isaac, whom you love. Each word presses on the father's heart. The surrounding peoples did sacrifice their children, and the Bible tells this story to show the opposite: the God of Abraham does not want the death of a child. The angel stops the knife, and Israel will never offer her sons. Yet the test is real, and Abraham's answer is a model of faith. He rises early in the morning. He walks for three days. He says to his servants, “we will worship, and then we will come back to you.” He believes, as the Letter to the Hebrews explains, that “God is able even to raise someone from the dead” (Hebrews 11:19). The most moving words are Isaac's: “The fire and the wood are here, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?” and Abraham's reply: “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” The Hebrew name he gives the mountain, Yahweh-yireh, means “The Lord will provide.” The Church has always heard in this story a shadow of the Father who “did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us” (Romans 8:32): the beloved son who carries the wood, the mountain in the land of Moriah, the three days, the lamb that God himself provides. Our Jewish elder brothers and sisters read this chapter, the Akedah, with deep reverence at the New Year, and we honour their reading as we offer ours. The Psalm gives the right answer to a test passed: “Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory.”

Matthew's Gospel now brings us home to Capernaum, “his own town.” Some people carry a paralysed man to Jesus on a bed, and the first thing Matthew tells us is that Jesus sees something: “When Jesus saw their faith.” The faith of the friends carries the sick man, and Jesus answers with a sentence that nobody asked for: “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.” The man had come for his legs; Jesus first heals his heart. Some scribes think, “This man is blaspheming,” and from their own point of view they are right: only God can forgive sins. Jesus does not deny it. He reads their thoughts and asks which is easier, to say “Your sins are forgiven” or “Stand up and walk.” Anyone can say the first, since no one can check it; the second can be seen. So he proves the invisible by the visible: “so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins,” he says to the paralytic, “Stand up, take your bed and go to your home.” And the man goes home carrying the bed that carried him. The crowds “glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.” The last words are in the plural, and the Church has always understood why: on Easter evening Jesus breathed on his apostles and said, “If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them” (John 20:23). This is why we confess our sins to a priest: the one who forgave the paralytic in Capernaum forgives us through the ministry of his Church (Catechism 1441–1442). And the lamb that God provided on Moriah is the One of whom John the Baptist said, “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!”
outline: Ask: when did someone's faith carry you, when you could not walk by yourself?
Abraham trusts that God can raise the dead, and God stops the knife.
Point 2 · God will provide the lamb
From Isaac's question to the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
Jesus heals the heart before the legs, and gives this authority to human beings.
live: Think of one person who is too weak to pray, to hope or to walk to Mass today. Carry them: call, visit, offer a lift, and pray for them by name.
If it has been a long time, choose a day this month for the sacrament of Reconciliation, and thank God for giving such authority to human beings.
2027-07-01.prayer: God of Abraham, you asked everything of your friend and you gave everything back to him. Give us a faith that trusts you on the mountain we do not understand, and teach us that you yourself provide the lamb. Lord Jesus, Lamb of God, who forgave the paralysed man and gave your Church the power to forgive, heal our hearts before our bodies, and make us friends who carry one another to you. Through your Precious Blood, wash away our sins and bring us home. Amen.
altar: At every Mass, before Communion, the priest holds up the Host and says: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who takes away the sins of the world. These are the words of John the Baptist, and behind them stand Isaac's question and Abraham's answer. The Father has provided the Lamb; the Lamb is placed on the altar; and the people answer with the words of another man who sought healing, the centurion of Capernaum: Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word and my soul shall be healed. In July, the month of the Precious Blood, we remember that the cup of Mass holds the blood of the covenant, poured out for the forgiveness of sins.

quick: God tests Abraham: he is to offer Isaac, the son of the promise; Abraham obeys in faith, and God provides a ram in his place.
The Lord swears an oath to Abraham: his descendants will be as many as the stars, and in his offspring all nations will be blessed.
Jesus sees the faith of the friends, forgives the paralysed man and heals him, to show that the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins.
2027-07-01.action: Carry one person in prayer today, and make a firm plan to go to confession this month.
2027-07-01.question: When God asks something I do not understand, do I say with Abraham, “Here I am,” and leave the lamb to him?

family.explain: Abraham loved his son Isaac very much. One day God asked Abraham to trust him in a very hard way. Abraham got up early, took wood, and walked up a mountain with Isaac. Isaac asked: where is the lamb? Abraham said: God himself will provide the lamb. And at the last moment God stopped Abraham and gave him a ram. God never wants a child to be hurt. He keeps his promises, and he provides. In the Gospel, some friends carried a man who could not walk to Jesus, and Jesus made him well.
family.intention: We thank God for those who carry us when we are weak. We pray for the sick, and for children who are afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “Who has carried us when things were hard? Whom can we help carry this week?”

illus: In a hill parish of Idukki, the monsoon had swollen the stream that separated one hamlet from the chapel. An old man who had been paralysed for years had said he would like to receive the Anointing of the Sick before he died. Four young men of the village made a cot out of two bamboo poles and a bedsheet, waded the stream chest-deep and carried him across, with the rain beating on their shoulders. The priest, who told the story afterwards, said the old man said little. He only kept repeating: they carried me. The priest thought of the roof in the Gospel and of the words, When Jesus saw their faith. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of Abraham, you provide what we need. Lord Jesus, forgive us and carry us to the Father. Amen.
share: God himself will provide the lamb (Genesis 22:8). Where in my life am I afraid that God will not provide?
Abraham said, “Here I am” (Genesis 22:1, 11). Do I say these words to God each morning?
When Jesus saw their faith (Matthew 9:2). Whose faith carried me, and whom can I carry?
pm.resp: Not to us, O Lord, but to your name give glory.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a place of forgiveness and healing.
For priests who hear confessions, and for those who have been away from the sacrament for a long time.
For people with paralysis, for their families and for those who care for them.
For parents who must trust God with a child they cannot protect.
For our group, that we may learn to carry one another.
pm.close: Father, you gave your Son for us, and in him you forgive us. Keep us in your covenant and make us trusting servants of your mercy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the first reading takes us up the mountain with Abraham and Isaac. It is a hard story, and we should not hurry past it. God asks Abraham for his son, his only son, whom he loves. Abraham does not argue. He rises early. He walks for three days. And on the way a boy asks the question every child would ask: where is the lamb? And the father who has no answer except trust says: God himself will provide the lamb, my son (Genesis 22:8).

At the last moment, the angel calls: Abraham, Abraham! Do not lay your hand on the boy (Genesis 22:12). The God of Abraham does not want children sacrificed. He wanted Abraham's heart, and Abraham gave it. And the story does not end with a test passed. It ends with a promise: in your offspring all the nations of the earth will gain blessing (Genesis 22:18). That offspring is Christ. Centuries later another Father would not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us (Romans 8:32), and John would point to Jesus and say: Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29). God did provide the lamb.

In the Gospel the lamb is already at work, in a small town by the lake. Friends bring a paralysed man, and Matthew says: when Jesus saw their faith (Matthew 9:2). Think of that. The friends say nothing in the story, and yet Jesus hears them. Their faith carried a man who could not walk. Who in your life has carried you? A mother, a grandmother, a teacher, a friend who prayed? And whom are you carrying?

Then Jesus says the unexpected words: Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven (Matthew 9:2). The paralytic's real burden was not his legs. Jesus heals the heart first, and then, to show that he has the right, he heals the body. And the crowds glorify God who had given such authority to human beings. Dear friends, that is the sacrament of Reconciliation. This month, the month of the Precious Blood, let us make the time. Let the Lamb of God lift the burden off our hearts, and then let us go home, like the paralytic, carrying the bed that carried us.
kids: Children, Abraham loved his son Isaac. One day God asked Abraham to trust him in a very hard way. Abraham got up early and walked to a mountain. Isaac asked: where is the lamb? Abraham said: God will provide the lamb. And God did! He stopped Abraham and gave a ram. God never wants a child to be hurt, and he always keeps his promise. In the Gospel, some friends carried a man who could not walk to Jesus. Jesus said: your sins are forgiven, and he made the man walk! Let us be good friends who help carry others.

intro: Theme: “God himself will provide the lamb.”
The test on Moriah, the Lamb whom God gives, and the friends whose faith carries the paralysed man to the One who forgives.

sub: Your son, your only son, whom you love.
Three days of walking in faith.
God is able to raise the dead.
q: Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on his son Isaac, and he himself carried the fire and the knife. So the two of them walked on together.
By faith Abraham, when put to the test, offered up Isaac.
points.apply: Name one thing God asks of you that you do not understand, and say to him this week, “Here I am.”

q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So the two of them walked on together.
The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him and declared, “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: At the Lamb of God at Mass, say in your heart the name of one person you wish to entrust to him.

q: who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases,
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Bring someone to Jesus this week: by prayer, an invitation to Mass, or a lift to confession.

concl: God tests Abraham, stops the knife, and promises that in his offspring all nations will be blessed; the Father later gives his own Son as the Lamb.
Jesus forgives the paralysed man because of his friends' faith, and shows that the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins.
2027-07-01.resolve: Go to confession this month, and carry one person to God in prayer every day this week.
